title: Paloma Business Plan Change Terms: Upgrades and Downgrades
content:
A plan change on a Paloma Business account is the owner's own decision; the agent explains its effect and the owner confirms it.

### Terms in force

**A. Status.** A plan can be changed only while the account status is active, as the account record shows.

**B. Upgrade.** An upgrade takes effect on the day it is made, and the business must meet the higher plan's months in business and have every document in the higher plan's list of required KYB documents logged.

**C. Downgrade timing.** A downgrade never takes effect mid-period: it is scheduled for the first day of the next billing period and applied then.

**D. Downgrade conditions.** A downgrade can be scheduled only when the account's active users (the owner plus every user added and not since removed) do not exceed the lower plan's largest number of active users, and the lower plan offers every submission channel the business has scheduled payouts on. Both are read from the account's records.

**E. What the new plan changes.** The allowance, limits, fees and seats of the new plan apply to payouts submitted after the change; the free payouts already granted for the period are not changed.

### Retired terms

- The former term under which, on an upgrade from a plan with upgrade proration whose current-period subscription fee was collected, the unused part of that fee was credited back by unused days over period days and the higher plan's fee for the same days was charged as a proration charge worked out the same way, is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for settling upgrade proration.
- The former term under which a downgrade or closure taking effect before the commitment end date carried an early termination fee of the plan's early-termination months times the committed plan's monthly fee is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for early termination charges.

### Condition table for scheduling a downgrade

| Account active | Active users within the lower plan's largest number | Lower plan offers every channel with scheduled payouts | Downgrade can be scheduled |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| No | any | any | No |
| Yes | No | any | No |
| Yes | any | No | No |

### Hypothetical cases

- An active account on Paloma Business Pro with 8 active users asks to move to Paloma Business Essentials, whose largest number of active users is 5: the downgrade cannot be scheduled.
- An account upgraded on the 12th of its billing period is on the higher plan from the 12th; payouts submitted from then on follow the higher plan's limits and fees, while the free payouts granted at the start of that period stay as granted.

superseded_clauses: On an upgrade from a plan whose upgrade_proration_enabled is true and whose subscription_fee for the current period was collected, the unused part of that fee is credited back as unused days over period days times the fee, rounded half up to the cent, where unused days run from the upgrade date to current_period_end inclusive; the higher plan's fee for the same unused days is charged at once as proration_charge, calculated the same way.
A downgrade or closure taking effect before commitment_end_date carries an early_termination_fee of early_termination_fee_months times the committed plan's monthly_fee_usd.
